Subject: Embedding architecture & migration follow-ups — next steps

Hi Samira / Imran — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap + recommended next steps from our side after reviewing the notes: 

Summary of what we heard
- Current usage: product search + short-form personalization + a lightweight reranker (annoy-based today).
- Scale: ~1.2M active documents, ~5–7k writes/day, peak query QPS ~80.
- Priority: accurate rerank + predictable latency under load.

Redwood recommendations (high level)
- Vector dimensionality: recommend 1536 for best recall on rerank workloads; 1024 if you need to trade some recall for ~20% storage/compute savings.
- Normalization: store L2-normalized vectors and use cosine on the ANN side to keep ranking stable across vector sources.
- Batching & ingestion: bulk reindex jobs in chunks (we usually suggest 4k–8k vectors per API batch for initial backfill, then 256–1024 for steady-state multi-threaded uploads depending on client throughput).
- Migration approach: dual-write to both systems + backfill using incremental snapshots to avoid downtime. We can help with scripts and a checkpointing strategy for resumable imports.
- Auth & SDK: OIDC-backed service accounts for server-side ingestion is recommended. Our Node + Python SDKs support short-lived tokens (rotate every 1h) and client-side caching for high throughput.

Attachments: I attached a short sizing guide and a migration checklist (redwood-embed-sizing.pdf, migration-playbook.xlsx) — they contain sample batch sizes and cost estimates.

Next concrete steps
1) Tech design review (30–45m) with your infra and search teams — propose Mon 5/17 11am PT or Tue 5/18 9am PT.
2) Share a sample of 5k documents (anonymized) for us to run a quick embedding/recall probe.
3) Confirm desired vector dim (1536 vs 1024) and any strict storage constraints.

Let me know which time works for the design review and whether the sample data is possible.

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright

Thanks Logan — appreciate the clear summary. A few answers and open questions from our side: 

Answers
- Current vector dims: our existing provider produces 768-d vectors.
- Indexing cadence: nightly bulk refresh plus frequent small updates (new products) throughout the day.
- Security: we require SSO-based service principals (Okta) and prefer short-lived tokens; we cannot share long-lived keys.
- Priority dims: accuracy for rerank > storage, so 1536 sounds reasonable, but need cost estimate.

Questions
1) If we move from 768 -> 1536, do you recommend re-embedding everything or is there a hybrid approach?
2) How would L2-normalization affect existing scoring if we migrate gradually?
3) Can your SDK handle chunked uploads with automatic retry and resume after failures?

We can do the design review Mon 5/17 11am PT. I'll invite our infra lead and search lead. I'll also start preparing a sandbox export of ~5k anonymized product rows.

Hi Samira / Imran — Marissa from Solutions Engineering here. Quick technical clarifications and a proposed low-risk migration pattern: 

On dimensionality & re-embedding
- Hybrid approach: keep existing 768-index live while running a parallel 1536 re-embed & index. Dual-query gateway (route to 1536 index for rerank tests; fallback to 768 for production) allows quantitative A/B before full cutover.
- Re-embedding is recommended for best quality; partial options (only re-embed high-impact content) are feasible to reduce compute.

Normalization & scoring
- L2-normalize on write; compute cosine at query time. When you compare scores across old vs new vectors, expect rank deltas — run our provided evaluation harness against held-out queries to quantify regressions.

Batching & ingestion patterns
- Bulk import: we recommend 4k vectors per chunk for the initial backfill jobs. Use parallel workers (4–8) and commit checkpoints after each chunk. Example steady-state: 512 vector batches with N concurrent upload workers tuned to keep client CPU/network saturated but below API concurrency limits.
- SDK behavior: Redwood SDKs provide chunking + automatic retry + resumable uploads. For very large backfills, we recommend using our CLI bulk-import tooling (covered in the migration-playbook.xlsx).

Auth & routing
- Okta OIDC: we support OIDC service principals and issue short-lived tokens. For server-side ingest, create a service client with token exchange and rotate tokens hourly.
- Request routing: you can pin read/write traffic by region via the routing header (x-rw-region) or configure our smart-routing policy to prefer region with lowest cost/latency and fall back on capacity.

Zero-downtime migration pattern (proposed)
1) Stand up 1536 index in parallel.
2) Dual-write new content to both indices.
3) Backfill historical content into 1536 index in chunks with checkpoints.
4) Run evaluation harness and A/B queries for 2–3 days.
5) Promote 1536 index, switch routing, and retire 768 after monitoring.

I'll attach an internal checklist and a sample evaluation query set (see attached migration-playbook.xlsx). If you want, Ben and I can run a short proof-of-concept on a 5k sample once you share the export.

- Redwood (Marissa / Ben): run initial sizing and cost delta (1536 vs 768) and share a short TCO slide.

Thanks — we'll be ready for Mon 11am PT.
